card.text: Explore Phoebe in 3D with cssEarth. Inspect Cassini imagery and shape-derived elevation on Saturn’s irregular outer moon.

introduction.text: Phoebe is a dark, cratered moon on a distant, retrograde orbit around Saturn. Cassini’s 2004 flyby revealed an irregular, ice-bearing surface. It may be a captured object from the outer solar system.

normal.title: SPC relative brightness model
normal.summary: Relative brightness from the 2023 Cassini shape/albedo model, normalized near one; not natural color or measured geometric albedo. Cells with fewer than five images or no maplet are marked missing. The 3,500-face display approximates the source shape; map detail is finer than the displayed geometry.

elevation.title: Q512 radial height model
elevation.summary: Q512 model radius minus a 106.5 km sphere, in km; not a geoid or independent altimetry. The paired 2023 model is less certain in poorly imaged regions; unsupported cells are marked. The 3,500-face display approximates the source shape; map detail is finer than the displayed geometry.

maplet-resolution.title: SPC maplet resolution
maplet-resolution.summary: Finest contributing SPC maplet spacing in each 1° cell, in m/vertex. Smaller values mean finer local input, not guaranteed height accuracy. Cells without a maplet are marked missing.

image-count.title: SPC image coverage
image-count.summary: Contributing image count in each 1° source cell. Zero remains visible; fewer than five images warrants caution. Many images can share viewing geometry, so count alone does not establish accuracy.

infrared.title: Cassini VIMS regional spectra · 11 June 2004
infrared.summary: False-color 2.02/1.59/1.28 µm infrared from a small 2004 flyby region. Gray grid marks gaps. Values retain illumination and archive filtering; placement has several-kilometer uncertainty.

ice-absorption.title: Cassini VIMS regional water-ice absorption · 11 June 2004
ice-absorption.summary: Near-2.02 µm ice absorption in a small, coarsely placed region. Gray grid marks gaps. Uncorrected values depend on viewing angle, grain size, noise and archive filtering; they do not measure ice abundance.
